name: fighter plane wrack world war II

tags.name: fighter plane wrack world war II
tags.notes: Coordinates match Irakleia/Herakleia island area (36.83N 25.42E). Likely the German Arado Ar196 seaplane (designation D1+EH), damaged by British aircraft escorting a convoy on 17 Sep 1943 and ditched near Naxos; crew Fritz Schaar and Herbert Schneider were picked up by German patrol boat UJ 2104 and held as POWs until 1948 (ww2wrecks.com). Found by fishermen at 91m in 1982 and relocated to Alimnia Bay, Irakleia at 9-11m depth. OSM recorded depth of 7m is within range. Not the Bristol Beaufighter TF Mk X JM225 (shot down 30 Oct 1943, 34m depth off Cape Kouroupas, Naxos - different location/depth). Also distinct from an unrelated second Arado Ar 196 wreck off Crete (Kalathas Bay, 64m depth, crashed 3 Aug 1943, crew Stienkemeier and Zacharias both killed, documented by grafasdiving.gr) - do not conflate the two aircraft. Re-audited 2026-08-03 via direct re-fetch of ww2wrecks.com; identification of this specific OSM node as the Irakleia Arado remains inferred from coordinates/depth, not an exact-name match (OSM entry carries no aircraft type).

tags.name: SS Probitas Shipwreck
tags.notes: LOCATION WARNING: Coordinates (39.87N, 20.01E) place this site in Saranda Bay, Albania, not Greece. PADI, Mapcarta, and the Albanian Diving Federation all list this as an Albania dive site. The OSM node may have been incorrectly assigned to the Greece dataset. Re-audited 2026-08-03: albaniandivingfederation.al (Albanian Diving Federation, new source found this pass) identifies the vessel as the former ANSALDO SAN GIORGIO PRIMO, built at the Ansaldo San Giorgio shipyard in Muggiano and completed March 1919 (construction no. 162), 5,084 tons, 115.2m long x 15.7m wide, renamed Probitas. Confirms the convoy/sister-ship narrative (motor ship Salvore and a transport from Dubac also attacked, both escaped to Italy) and Ju 87 Stuka attack while moored at dock after a mechanical breakdown. DATE CONFLICT: Albanian Diving Federation and OSM both state 25 September 1943; a lower-authority Medium blog post states 26 September 1943 with a different framing (ship evacuating troops, six Italian soldiers killed) that could not be corroborated elsewhere - the 25 September 1943 date (Albanian Diving Federation, OSM) is retained as better-sourced. DEPTH CONFLICT: sources vary - PADI states 3-22m, silver-sky.club states 20-30m, Albanian Diving Federation states 3-25m; depth updated from 18m to 25m (max reported by the two most-specific sources) and the range is described in the markdown rather than a single figure. blog.mares.com (previously cited) returned repeated 503 errors during re-audit and was dropped from the source list; replaced with albaniandivingfederation.al.

tags.name: Uçak Batığı
tags.notes: Turkish name meaning 'airplane wreck'. Coordinates (36.987N, 27.432E) sit almost exactly on Karaada (Black Island) off the Bodrum peninsula, Turkey, not in Greek waters - this OSM node was very likely misassigned to the Greece dataset. Re-audited 2026-08-03 with 4 independent Turkish sources (previously-cited kosdiving.com was dropped - re-fetched directly and it does not mention this site or 'Aksona' by name and was never a valid source). All 4 sources agree this is a Douglas C-47 Dakota, formerly Turkish Air Force (used to deploy paratroops over Cyprus in 1974), decommissioned and donated to BOSAD, intentionally sunk 1 July 2008 in Paçoz Cove near Karaada as an artificial reef. In 2010 currents broke the wreck into two pieces; the hangar/tail section drifted deeper. Depths across sources: sualtigazetesi.com 16-28m pre-break, hangar/tail now 28-34m; thediversclub.com.tr gives engine ~17m, cockpit ~23m, fuselage ~34m, max 36m; aquapro-turkey.com and zentacle.com give 17-32m/19-33m. DEPTH CORRECTED from 72m (OSM recorded, inconsistent with every documented source for a wreck of this name in this strait) to 34m, matching the consensus 3-36m multi-part wreck profile. This is not a technical/trimix dive; recreational Advanced divers can reach the deepest sections. Marine life per thediversclub.com.tr: groupers, moray eels, dentex, leerfish, lionfish, crabs, lobsters, tritons, nudibranchs, posidonia beds.

tags.name: Aksona
tags.notes: Aksona is named after 'Aksona Mehmet', a famous sponge hunter from Bodrum. Coordinates (36.96N, 27.49E) are in Turkish waters near Bodrum, not Greek waters. Site starts at 3m, slopes to 20m then wall drops to 30-35m. Known for Phoenician amphoras and a ship's anchor at 13.5m depth (justgottadive.com). Re-audited 2026-08-03: kosdiving.com (previously cited) was re-fetched directly and does not mention Aksona - dropped as an invalid source and replaced with justgottadive.com (confirmed direct match) and divessi.com/MyDiveGuide 'Aksona Bay' listing. Operated by Bodrum-based Turkish dive operators (~50 min boat ride). Site type remains wall based on documented drop-off profile.
